title: Mathlib Import
content: The single import `Mathlib.Tactic` brings in Lean's standard tactic library, which provides automation tools like `ring`, `push_neg`, `by_cases`, and `calc`. This is the most common import for Lean proofs and gives access to hundreds of proof automation tactics without pulling in specific mathematical theories.
mathContext: Mathlib.Tactic provides decision procedures for commutative rings, linear arithmetic, and propositional logic

title: Module Documentation
content: The module-level docstring describes this file as a pedagogical collection of basic proof techniques. It catalogs the tactics demonstrated (case analysis, calculational proofs, ring arithmetic, function application) and lists dependencies. This structured documentation follows Lean Genius conventions for making proofs discoverable and self-documenting.
mathContext: Documents proof techniques: `by_cases` for case splits, `calc` for chains of equalities/inequalities, `ring` for polynomial arithmetic

title: Namespace Declaration
content: The `namespace Sqrt2` declaration scopes all definitions and theorems under the `Sqrt2` prefix, avoiding name collisions with Mathlib or other proof files. In Lean 4, namespaces also enable dot notation — `Sqrt2.square_nonneg` can be accessed as `.square_nonneg` when the `Sqrt2` namespace is open.

title: Non-negativity of Squares
content:
**Theorem**: For any integer $n$, $n^2 \geq 0$.

The proof proceeds by case analysis on the sign of $n$:

**Case $n \geq 0$**: Apply `mul_nonneg h h` — the product of two non-negative numbers is non-negative. This is a single-step application of a Mathlib lemma.

**Case $n < 0$**: The proof uses `push_neg` to convert the negated hypothesis into $n < 0$, then derives $n \leq 0$ and $0 \leq -n$. The `calc` block rewrites $n \cdot n = (-n) \cdot (-n)$ using the `ring` tactic (which solves polynomial identities automatically), then applies `mul_nonneg` to $-n \geq 0$.

This proof pattern — splitting on sign and reducing the negative case to the positive one — is a template used throughout number theory and real analysis.
mathContext: $\forall n \in \mathbb{Z},\; n \cdot n \geq 0$. The key identity is $n \cdot n = (-n) \cdot (-n)$, which holds in any commutative ring.

title: Implication Transitivity
content:
**Theorem**: Implications compose — $(P \to Q) \to (Q \to R) \to (P \to R)$.

The proof demonstrates **backward reasoning**, the most characteristic pattern in Lean:

1. `intro hpq hqr hp` — introduce three hypotheses: $P \to Q$, $Q \to R$, and $P$
2. `apply hqr` — to prove $R$ (our goal), it suffices to prove $Q$ (since $Q \to R$)
3. `apply hpq` — to prove $Q$ (our new goal), it suffices to prove $P$ (since $P \to Q$)
4. `exact hp` — we have $P$ as hypothesis

This is the formal version of a syllogism: chaining two implications. In Lean's type theory, this is function composition — `imp_trans` is essentially `fun f g x => g (f x)`.
mathContext: $(P \to Q) \to (Q \to R) \to (P \to R)$. In the Curry-Howard correspondence, this is function composition: $g \circ f$.

title: Namespace Closure
content: The `end Sqrt2` closes the namespace opened at line 30. All theorems defined within — `square_nonneg` and `imp_trans` — are now accessible as `Sqrt2.square_nonneg` and `Sqrt2.imp_trans` from outside the namespace. This clean scoping ensures the pedagogical examples don't pollute the global namespace.
mathContext: Closes the `Sqrt2` scope; theorems are fully qualified as `Sqrt2.square_nonneg` and `Sqrt2.imp_trans`
